source.title: TaoType: Predicting Fine-Grained Typing Intent for Faster Search
source.authors: Yi-Peng Yu; Yichen Yuan; Chengxiao Feng; Xu Liu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper is present and readable, with minor PDF extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper briefly compares a training-data-duration result for its own compact query-intent classifier to scaling laws, but does not test language-model pretraining loss, model-size or compute scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a sweep over training-data duration for TaoType and says performance peaks at one week, with precision and accuracy declining when more historical data is added. These are task-classification metrics for a compact CRF model, not held-out language-model pretraining loss or any other behavior measured by V1–V7. The model baselines, feature ablations, device tests, and online A/B results likewise do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds a ~78 KB CRF query-intent classifier. Its only scaling-related result is a sweep of training-data duration from 1 day to 1 month, with task precision, recall and accuracy as the measures. It does not measure language-model loss, parameter or compute scaling, power-law fits, or downstream performance as a function of LM scale. Its mention of Kaplan et al. is an analogy, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that TaoType predicts query completeness well offline (0.7936/0.8196/0.7742) and cuts online response time by about 640 ms. They also say that, for compact dynamic-intent models, recent data beats larger older data, which they liken loosely to Kaplan et al.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a client-side CRF framework for query-intent prediction; it does not reproduce the language-model scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: For TaoType’s classification performance, training-data duration matters: the reported precision, recall, and accuracy peak at one week, and precision and accuracy decline with further data.

fits_no_version.finding: TaoType (CRF, ~78 KB) peaks at one week of training data (P/R/A 0.7936/0.8196/0.7742). Precision and accuracy decline with 2w–1m of data; the authors attribute this to distribution-shift noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For compact classifiers on non-stationary behavioural data, adding older training data beyond a recent window can lower task performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Industry Track (2026)
record.problems: No evidence on the claim versions; the relevant analogy is limited to a non-language-model classifier and task metrics, and exact post-one-week values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were extracted because the remaining reported results concern query-intent classification, features, devices, or online search latency rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All: LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
All: architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
All: power-law form in other modalities or regimes. The data sweep is on a CRF classifier and no power law is fitted.
All: downstream performance vs LM scale or loss.
All: dependence of fitted exponents on setup.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification is upheld. The Kaplan citation is only an analogy. Recall at windows beyond 1w is not described in the text, and values for 2w–1m can be read only from Figure 3.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute for language models.
Whether small-run power-law fits predict much larger language-model runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations as compute changes.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior outside text pretraining or under other training regimes.
Downstream task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.note: The paper says precision reaches its peak at 1 week and declines with further data. This is a compact query-intent classifier result, not language-model pretraining loss.
rows.check: The measure is classification precision for a non-LM CRF classifier under training-data duration, not held-out LM loss. The decline after 1 week comes from data recency and distribution shift, not from a parameter bottleneck in an LM. The 'baseline' is the peak value at 1w; values for 2w–1m appear only in Figure 3 and are not given in the text.
